summary: The mating finder's foundations exist and are enforced on the server. Migration 0053 is purely additive: seven new enums, three ADD VALUEs (the MATING species gate, the MATING_FINDER settings group, the MATING_FINDER_SUBSCRIPTION payment service) and three versioned tables. A plan version (owner or kennel, one/three/six/twelve months, title, price, active-animal capacity, optional sale window, suspension policy that never refunds) is written once; publishing names the version the operator saw, archives it in the same transaction and a unique partial index keeps one published version per slot, so a stale panel and two simultaneous publishes each end with one winner. The price lives on the version itself and createBatch reads it through a fifth price source, FINDER_PLAN, shaped like the club rule version; an unset price shows the plan but refuses checkout with a Persian operator reason, and zero is rejected. Nothing is seeded: no plan, no price, no capacity. Buying and renewing reuse createBatch/startAttempt/verifyAttempt unchanged; the checkout copies the entire plan version onto the period, so a later price or capacity edit moves nothing already bought; activation runs inside the verifying transaction under the account row lock and starts where the live chain ends, so a renewal never overlaps, a replayed callback does nothing, an amount mismatch activates nothing, and two payments verified at the same moment queue one after the other — all proven against a real database. A checkout replaced by a newer one is SUPERSEDED rather than cancelled, so if its old batch is paid anyway the money still buys the period it priced. Expiry is read from ends_at with no scheduler; an expired subscription falls back to the managed free-owner capacity, never to 'no limit', the Phase 3 seller-plan defect deliberately not repeated. Breed-and-sex rules are versioned the same way (species default or breed-specific, min/max age, cooldown in days or months, kinship degree, WARN or BLOCK) and the seed writes only the confirmed baseline once: dog male 14 days, female 6 months, warning only; ages and kinship thresholds stay unset. Nine kill switches, the request expiry (7 days), contract OTP bounds, media bounds and the free-owner capacity are managed settings in the MATING_FINDER group, writable by the superadmin alone, every switch starting closed. The access matrix is a server answer: a subscribed owner's profile is public, a free owner's is visible only to subscribers while the free-pool switch is open, the owner always sees their own, and a pair needs both KYC approvals and at least one live subscription. Seven Finder capabilities sit on the existing operational contexts; configuration is the superadmin's alone, no other context holds more than three, and none reads a chat or a contract body. The superadmin page /admin/mating-finder publishes and withdraws plans, publishes rules, opens species and shows the switches; /account/mating-finder shows standing, capacity, plans the account may buy (a kennel plan needs an approved kennel), history and which registered animals carry an official microchip. The upgrade rehearsal now has a real Phase 3 boundary and a separate Phase 4 step, 54/54. The full product run found one intended change to a Phase 3 expectation (three markets per species now) and four transient 'Connection terminated unexpectedly' failures in suites this prompt does not touch; the expectation was updated and all five suites re-ran green.

limitations: No real price, capacity, age range or kinship threshold exists: all are PRODUCT_DECISION_OPEN or operational data and stay unset until a superadmin publishes them; with nothing published, owners see no plan for sale.
The capacity race test counts a synthetic audit row under the account lock, because the mating_profile table arrives in PROMPT-003; PROMPT-003 must repeat it against real profile activation.

The account page lists registered animals of an open species with an official-microchip badge; it activates no profile and says so. Profile eligibility (KYC, fertility declaration, life status, photos) is PROMPT-003.

Two payment attempts on one pending batch can still both be paid at the gateway (platform behaviour of startAttempt, DEC-0217 section 12); the finder effect activates only once, but the second charge would need a manual refund. Not fixed here because it changes every paid service.
Suspension policy is recorded on each plan and snapshotted on each period, but suspension itself is PROMPT-007.
The subscription-activated notification is in-app only and sits behind finder.flag.notifications, which starts closed.
No real gateway: the browser run used the development gateway page and the database run a test gateway; neither is provider evidence.
Four full-run failures were transient connection terminations in untouched suites and were re-run individually rather than by repeating the 20-minute full product suite.
